_comment: Source registry for the danger-signal study. Anchors are published observations with their original assay and sampling definitions, not interchangeable latent release parameters. Local source PDFs are gitignored.

datasets.source: Yamaguchi S, Sato S, Toriya M, Tsuji A. Jpn J Antibiot 1999;52(1):41-56. PMID 10202687 (in Japanese; figures are language-independent).
datasets.why: Paired viable-count and free-LPS trajectories could inform an observation-model fit after digitisation. Published summaries alone do not identify latent per-CFU release yields.
extract: For each agent and each concentration (1/4x, 1x MIC and any others shown): free LPS (ng/mL) vs time over 0-8 h.

The MATCHED viable count (log10 CFU/mL) vs time for the same condition. Without the matched count the yield per CFU killed is not identifiable -- this pairing is the whole reason this paper is priority 1.
The pharmacokinetic autosimulation arm: free LPS and viable count vs time over 0-8 h for each agent, plus the simulated concentration-time profile if given.
RESOLVED 2026-10-14, see full_text below: the starting inoculum is 1e6 CFU/mL, NOT the 1e8 this study assumed. Every per-CFU yield scales off it.
The LPS assay used and its standard (Limulus/LAL vs ELISA; EU/mL vs ng/mL conversion, if stated). RESOLVED: Limulus colour KY test (Wako), each sample measured twice and averaged.

full_text.obtained: 2026-10-14 from J-Stage, open access (jiyu/free), DOI 10.11553/antibiotics1968b.52.41. PDF kept in docs/article_pdfs/52_41.pdf (gitignored).
full_text.inoculum_quote: Methods II.4: cells grown 18 h on SDA, suspended in saline, added to 10 mL of STB to 1e6 cfu/mL, shaken at 37 C; drug added at 1/4, 1 and 4 MIC AT THE START of culture; 1 mL sampled at 2, 4 and 6 h. Methods II.5 (simulation): inoculated into 100 mL STB to 1e6 cfu/mL, pre-cultured 3 h, then the simulated plasma profile was applied.
full_text.viable_counts_fig2_log10: All arms start at 6.0, confirming the 1e6 inoculum. Ceftazidime 1x MIC falls to about 3.7 by 4 h; the untreated control rises to about 7.9 by 6 h. No treated arm exceeds about 6.4 at any time.
full_text.consequence: The source inoculum is 1e6 CFU/mL. Inoculum or net CFU loss cannot substitute for integrated drug-induced killing. Untreated free LPS is appreciable, so background release and clearance require an observation model. Preserve the point versus sampling-mean distinction; do not form an ISP:beta-lactam yield ratio from unmatched summaries.
full_text.corroboration: At 6 h the untreated control (about 6000 ng/mL) released MORE free LPS than every treated arm including the sub-MIC ones. This is independent support for the study's no-within-agent-trade-off result, from the same figure.
full_text.isepamicin_anchor_estimand: The 28 +/- 2 ng/mL figure is the MEAN of the 2, 4 and 6 h values at 1x MIC (Japanese abstract: 1 MIC ni okeru 2, 4, 6 jikan go no LPS ryou no heikin chi), not a 6 h reading. The piperacillin and ceftazidime anchors ARE single 4 h readings.

qualitative: At 1/4 x MIC, piperacillin and ceftazidime did NOT reduce colony counts and induced MORE free LPS release than at 1x MIC -- the kill-independent (filamentation) pathway.
Imipenem: rapid killing with less LPS release; free LPS rose at 8 h with regrowth.
Total LPS released over 8 h in the PK simulation: isepamicin < imipenem < ceftazidime < piperacillin.

datasets.notes: Full text obtained. Endpoints are assay-scale LPS observations with different time operators, not per-CFU yield measurements. No absolute release parameter can be fitted from these summaries alone. See src/analysis/yield_observations.py for point versus sampling-mean operators.

datasets.organism: P. aeruginosa (smooth- and rough-LPS mutant isolates)
datasets.source: Jackson JJ, Kropp H. J Infect Dis 1992;165(6):1033-41. doi:10.1093/infdis/165.6.1033 (PMID 1583320).
datasets.why: Held-out Layer-1 validation: a different laboratory, assay and LPS phenotype from Yamaguchi, and the source of the direct observation that sub-MIC ceftazidime induces filamentation and LPS release WITHOUT significant lysis. Also carries a mouse-lethality readout of the filtrates, which links released danger signal to an in-vivo consequence.
extract: Free LPS vs time (0-8 h) for ceftazidime and imipenem, at sub-MIC, 1x, 2x and 50x MIC, for BOTH the smooth- and rough-LPS isolates.
Matched colony counts for the same conditions (the paper reports imipenem reducing counts ~2 log more than ceftazidime at 2 h at sub-MIC levels).
The mouse lethality of culture filtrates (LD50 or percentage mortality) against the measured endotoxin concentration.
Starting inoculum and assay volume from the Methods.
MICs of both agents for both isolates (the abstract states they are equivalent).

qualitative: Sub-MIC ceftazidime induced filamentation and LPS release without significant bacterial lysis.
LPS released at sub-MIC ceftazidime matched the amounts at 1x, 2x and 50x MIC, and exceeded imipenem at up to 100x its MIC.
Filtrate lethality in mice tracked the in-vitro endotoxin results.

datasets.notes: Held out from all fitting. The 10-40x ratio is the single most important number in the study: it is the effect size the whole hypothesis rests on, and it is measured between two BACTERICIDAL agents with equivalent MICs -- which is what makes the cidal/static classification the wrong axis.

datasets.source: Haudek SB, Natmessnig BE, Furst W, Bahrami S, Schlag G, Redl H. Shock 2003;20(5):431-6. doi:10.1097/01.shk.0000090843.66556.74 (PMID 14560107).
datasets.why: Sets the Layer-2 operating range: an LPS dose-response spanning ~6 orders of magnitude (1 mg, 0.1 mg and 4 ng per kg) with TNF, IL-6 and IL-8 kinetics AND measured LPS clearance. The acceptance test that the cytokine layer is not saturated can only be made quantitative against a dose-response of this span.
extract: TNF, IL-6 and IL-8 (pg/mL) vs time for EACH of the three bolus doses, plus the 1.5 mg/kg 30-min infusion arm.
The measured plasma LPS clearance curve -- this is the k_ds the pilot currently takes from a 3 min half-life assumption.
Baseline (pre-challenge) cytokine concentrations, needed for the IL6_baseline parameter.

qualitative: Cytokine, haemodynamic and haematologic kinetics resembled human endotoxemia QUALITATIVELY.
Baboons required an ~1e4-fold HIGHER initial LPS dose than humans to develop the same manifestations.

datasets.notes: SPECIES-SCALE CAVEAT, and it is the important one: the paper itself reports that baboons need ~1e4x the human LPS dose. The Hill SHAPE (slope, span, kinetics) may be taken from this paper, but DS50 must NOT be taken from it on an absolute human scale. The pilot anchors DS50 on human experimental endotoxemia instead (4 ng/kg IV ~= 93 pg/mL plasma, a clear but submaximal response) and treats 30-1000 pg/mL as the uncertainty range. A human whole-blood or monocyte LPS-TNF concentration-response is the better absolute anchor and should be added as a separate Layer-2 dataset.

_schema.ds_release: Long-format CSV: agent,concentration_xMIC,time_h,series,value. series in {free_lps_ng_mL, cell_associated_lps_ng_mL, log10_cfu_mL, filament_fraction}. One row per digitized point. Blank/# lines ignored, so a header-only stub reports NO_DATA.
_schema.ds_cytokine: Long-format CSV: dose_label,time_h,series,value. series in {lps_pg_mL, TNF_pg_mL, IL6_pg_mL, IL8_pg_mL}.

_note: Nominal release coefficients are historical scale conventions. Quantitative fitting requires paired trajectories and the correct observation operators; see yield_observations.py and joint_robustness.json.
